results.name: periodic_penalty_given_alt
results.description: OLS coefficient of chose_left on the periodicity-indicator difference (right periodic minus left periodic, e.g. HTHTHTHT, HHTTHHTT), controlling for alternation and squared-distance differences; t_observed > null_mean means people reject regular repeating patterns more than the model predicts.

results.name: longest_run_coef_given_alt
results.description: OLS coefficient of chose_left on the longest-run-length difference (normalised by length, right minus left), controlling for alternation difference and squared-distance difference; t_observed > null_mean means long streaks are penalised beyond what alternation rate explains.

results.name: perfect_alternation_choice
results.description: Among trials where exactly one sequence is perfectly alternating (HTHT.../THTH...), the proportion choosing that sequence; t_observed < null_mean means the model over-predicts preference for perfect alternation (people see it as too regular).

results.name: left_choice_rate
results.description: Overall proportion of Left choices; t_observed > null_mean means a left-side response bias the side-symmetric model does not produce.

results.name: equal_alt_balance_pref
results.description: Among trials whose two sequences have identical alternation rates, the proportion choosing the sequence with the more balanced H/T count (ties in balance excluded); the model predicts 0.5, so t_observed > null_mean means people use H/T balance, which the model ignores.

results.name: balance_coef_given_alt
results.description: OLS coefficient of chose_left on the H/T imbalance difference (imbalance_right - imbalance_left), controlling for alternation-rate difference and its square-distance-from-0.6 difference; t_observed > null_mean means people favour balanced sequences more than the alternation-only model predicts.

results.name: pair_consensus_extremity
results.description: Mean over unordered stimulus pairs of |P(choose the lexicographically smaller sequence) - 0.5|; t_observed > null_mean means people agree on pairs more strongly than the model's heterogeneity/noise allows, lower means the model is overconfident.
results.code:
# name: pair_consensus_extremity
# description: Mean over unordered stimulus pairs of |P(choose the lexicographically smaller sequence) - 0.5|; t_observed > null_mean means people agree on pairs more strongly than the model's heterogeneity/noise allows, lower means the model is overconfident.
def test_statistic(df):
    a = df["sequence_a"].to_numpy(); b = df["sequence_b"].to_numpy()
    y = df["chose_left"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    swap = a > b
    key = np.where(swap, b + "|" + a, a + "|" + b)
    chose_first = np.where(swap, 1 - y, y)
    p = pd.Series(chose_first).groupby(key).mean()
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(p.to_numpy() - 0.5)))

results.name: participant_left_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across participants of each participant's Left-choice rate; t_observed > null_mean means individual side biases (or response noise heterogeneity) the model lacks.
